chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Playing in the pit band for the carnival show
summary: The band played for the stage acts and backed the Young family saxophone act, with Cootie reading the parts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How about that. That's funny, isn't it? Well, listen. If you were blowing with them for about three months, that's one time when you came to know the library, because they must have played everything that was -- all the standards and everything, huh?
Yeah.
What other kinds of things did they play? I mean, they didn't play march music or anything did they?
No. Well, I tell you, we played for the people in the show. They had a show, a stage show.
Oh, you played for the acts.
We played for the acts. And we played -- then Lester, then, would go on the stage with his father and his mother and Irma and Lee with the saxophone act.
Yeah.
And we would stay down there in the pit with the drums and the trumpet and things, to back them up.
I see. Yeah. Yeah, I see. They were part of the act, and they were part of the pit band.
Yeah.
Yeah, I see. Well, was there anybody else in the pit band?
Yeah. I can't remember them.
But some other instruments, huh?
Yeah.
A couple of other people.
I can't remember them.
No. But probably like bass and --
Yeah.
-- guitar and stuff, or maybe even banjo, huh?
Yeah. I can't remember nobody but, you know, the family.
Yeah. Well, so you didn't actually get
up on the stage with them, then?
No. But you were cutting that music, though. You were reading.
Uh-huh.
Which must have surprised them, huh?
No, but he -- see, that old man liked me. Lester's father liked me from the get-go. He liked my playing.
Yeah.
And that's the reason why he wanted me.
Yeah.
And my father talked to him. Yes, he wanted me very badly. So -- cause that's how I happened to --
